fields.lead: Pushing codes and bounds toward practical limits at short block lengths and in networks, and using information-theoretic ideas to understand learning and compression by neural models.

papers.title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
papers.why: Defined information, entropy and channel capacity and proved that reliable communication up to capacity is possible. Every code and every rate bound is still measured against Shannon's limits.

papers.title: Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
papers.why: Proposed sparse parity-check codes with iterative decoding, then largely forgotten for 30 years. Rediscovered, LDPC codes now carry Wi-Fi, 5G data and satellite links.

papers.title: Noiseless Coding of Correlated Information Sources
papers.why: Showed correlated sources can be compressed separately as efficiently as jointly. The basis of distributed compression and network information theory.

papers.title: The Wire-Tap Channel
papers.why: Showed secure communication is possible without keys when the eavesdropper's channel is worse. Physical-layer security in wireless research grows from this model.

papers.title: A Universal Algorithm for Sequential Data Compression
papers.why: Gave a dictionary compressor that needs no model of the source. LZ77 descendants (gzip, zstd) still compress most data on the internet.

papers.title: Modeling by Shortest Data Description
papers.why: Introduced the minimum description length principle: the best model is the one that compresses the data most. The compression view of learning is again central to how people think about large models.

papers.title: The Information Bottleneck Method
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 37th Annual Allerton Conference on Communication, Control and Computing
papers.why: Framed learning a representation as keeping only the information relevant to a target. Its use to explain deep learning is still disputed.

papers.title: Network Information Flow
papers.why: Showed that mixing data at network nodes can beat routing. Network coding underlies distributed storage codes and multicast research.

papers.title: Channel Polarization: A Method for Constructing Capacity-Achieving Codes for Symmetric Binary-Input Memoryless Channels
papers.why: Gave the first explicit low-complexity codes provably achieving capacity. Polar codes are in the 5G control channel and an active research area.

papers.title: Channel Coding Rate in the Finite Blocklength Regime
papers.why: Showed how far below capacity you must operate with short blocks. Essential for low-latency communication and now the standard benchmark for short codes.

more.title: Near Shannon Limit Error-Correcting Coding and Decoding: Turbo-Codes
more.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC '93)
more.why: Showed iterative decoding could come within a fraction of a decibel of capacity, which few thought practical. Its iterative-decoding idea reshaped coding theory and inference.

more.title: Capacity of Multi-Antenna Gaussian Channels
more.why: Showed capacity grows roughly linearly with the number of antennas. It is the theory behind MIMO and massive MIMO in current wireless systems.

more.title: The Capacity of Low-Density Parity-Check Codes under Message-Passing Decoding
more.why: Introduced density evolution to compute the noise thresholds of iterative decoders. It is still the main tool for designing LDPC codes.

more.title: Compressed Sensing
more.why: Showed sparse signals can be recovered from far fewer measurements than classical sampling requires. It changed medical imaging and signal processing and connects to high-dimensional statistics.

more.title: Interference Alignment and Degrees of Freedom of the K-User Interference Channel
more.why: Showed each user can get half the spectrum regardless of how many users interfere, by aligning interference. It reshaped multi-user wireless theory.

more.title: Fundamental Limits of Caching
more.why: Showed that coding cached content gives gains that grow with network size. It opened a large field on caching and coded distributed computing.

more.title: List Decoding of Polar Codes
more.why: Made polar codes competitive at practical lengths with list decoding plus CRC. This step led to their adoption in 5G.

more.title: End-to-End Optimized Image Compression
more.why: Trained a neural image codec directly on the rate-distortion objective. It launched learned compression, which now rivals standard codecs.

more.title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Generalization Capability of Learning Algorithms
more.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
more.why: Bounded generalization error by the mutual information between training data and the learned model. A main line of information-theoretic learning theory.

more.title: Language Modeling Is Compression
more.why: Showed large language models are strong general-purpose compressors, even of images and audio. It makes the old equivalence between prediction and compression concrete for modern AI.

fields.lead: Handling bounded rationality and behavioral deviations, learning and computing equilibria, and designing mechanisms, information and AI agents for strategic settings.

papers.title: Non-Cooperative Games
papers.why: Defined equilibrium for any finite game and proved it exists. Still the central solution concept, and its computation and plausibility remain open questions.

papers.title: Games with Incomplete Information Played by 'Bayesian' Players, I–III
papers.why: Made games with private information tractable by modeling players' types and beliefs. Auctions, signaling and information design all use this framework.
papers.note: Published in three parts, 1967–68; year given for Part I.

papers.title: The Logic of Animal Conflict
papers.why: Introduced the evolutionarily stable strategy, bringing game theory into biology. Evolutionary game theory and learning dynamics still build on it.

papers.title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
papers.why: Documented systematic violations of expected utility and modeled them with reference points and loss aversion. Behavioral economics still argues over and extends it.

papers.title: Optimal Auction Design
papers.why: Characterized revenue-maximizing auctions with virtual values. Mechanism design, including automated and learned auctions, starts here.

papers.title: Correlated Equilibrium as an Expression of Bayesian Rationality
papers.why: Showed correlated equilibrium follows from common priors and rationality. It is the concept learning algorithms actually converge to, which keeps it central.

papers.title: A Simple Adaptive Procedure Leading to Correlated Equilibrium
papers.why: Showed simple regret-matching players converge to correlated equilibrium. Regret minimization now drives the strongest game-playing AI.

papers.title: How Bad Is Selfish Routing?
papers.why: Bounded how much selfish behavior costs a network compared with central control. The 'price of anarchy' became a core tool of algorithmic game theory.

papers.title: The Complexity of Computing a Nash Equilibrium
papers.why: Showed computing Nash equilibria is PPAD-complete, so likely intractable. Raises doubts about Nash as a prediction and motivates other concepts.

papers.title: Superhuman AI for Multiplayer Poker
papers.why: Pluribus beat top professionals at six-player poker, where equilibrium guarantees break down. A milestone for AI in imperfect-information, multi-agent settings.

more.title: College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage
more.why: Defined stable matching and gave the deferred-acceptance algorithm. It runs school choice and medical residency matching today and anchors market-design research.

more.title: Quantal Response Equilibria for Normal Form Games
more.why: Replaced exact best responses with noisy, probabilistic ones in an equilibrium model. It is the standard model fitted to laboratory game data and in multi-agent AI.

more.title: A Theory of Fairness, Competition, and Cooperation
more.why: Modeled people as disliking unequal payoffs to explain fair and cooperative behavior in experiments. It remains a main model of social preferences in behavioral economics.

more.title: The Redesign of the Matching Market for American Physicians: Some Engineering Aspects of Economic Design
more.why: Showed how matching theory was adapted to redesign a real labor market. It became the template for market design as an engineering discipline.

more.title: A Cognitive Hierarchy Model of Games
more.why: Modeled players as reasoning only a limited number of steps about others. It is a leading account of bounded rationality in strategic settings.

more.title: Regret Minimization in Games with Incomplete Information
more.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS)
more.why: Introduced counterfactual regret minimization for large imperfect-information games. It is the algorithm behind superhuman poker AI and much multi-agent research.

more.title: Bayesian Persuasion
more.why: Asked how a sender should design what information to reveal in order to influence a decision-maker. It started information design, now a major area of economic theory.

more.title: Bayes Correlated Equilibrium and the Comparison of Information Structures in Games
more.why: Characterized every outcome achievable across all possible information structures in a game. A core tool of information design and robust predictions.

more.title: Optimal Auctions through Deep Learning
more.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML)
more.why: Used neural networks to learn near-optimal multi-item auctions where theory has no closed form. A leading example of machine learning applied to mechanism design.

more.authors: Meta FAIR Diplomacy Team, Bakhtin et al.
more.title: Human-Level Play in the Game of Diplomacy by Combining Language Models with Strategic Reasoning
more.why: Cicero combined a language model with strategic planning to negotiate and cooperate with human players. It is a frontier example of AI in mixed cooperative-competitive games.
more.note: Credited to the Meta Fundamental AI Research Diplomacy Team (FAIR) with Bakhtin and many others; exact author-line format not confirmed.

fields.lead: Moving beyond static pairwise graphs to multilayer, temporal and higher-order networks, and testing which structural claims hold up against careful statistical inference.

papers.title: The Strength of Weak Ties
papers.why: Argued that acquaintances, not close friends, bridge groups and carry new information. Still tested on large-scale data, including in recent field experiments on job mobility.

papers.title: Collective Dynamics of 'Small-World' Networks
papers.why: Showed that a few random shortcuts make a clustered network small-world. Launched modern network science and remains a standard model.

papers.title: Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks
papers.why: Proposed growth with preferential attachment to explain heavy-tailed degrees. Its claim that real networks are 'scale-free' is still debated.

papers.title: Error and Attack Tolerance of Complex Networks
papers.why: Showed hub-dominated networks survive random failures but break under targeted attack. Robustness analysis of infrastructure still begins here.

papers.title: Random Graphs with Arbitrary Degree Distributions and Their Applications
papers.why: Gave generating-function methods for random graphs with any degree distribution. The configuration model is the standard null model and analytical tool for spreading and percolation.

papers.title: Epidemic Spreading in Scale-Free Networks
papers.why: Showed epidemics can spread without a threshold on heavy-tailed networks. Network epidemiology, used in COVID-19 modeling, grew from this.

papers.title: Modularity and Community Structure in Networks
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.why: Gave the modularity measure and a spectral method to find communities. Modularity is still the most used community criterion, and its limits are well studied.

papers.title: Catastrophic Cascade of Failures in Interdependent Networks
papers.why: Showed coupled networks such as power and communication grids can collapse abruptly. Central to work on systemic risk and resilience.

papers.authors: Kivelä, Arenas, Barthelemy, Gleeson, Moreno & Porter
papers.title: Multilayer Networks
papers.why: Unified the many ways of representing networks with multiple types of links. The reference framework for multilayer analysis.

papers.authors: Battiston, Cencetti, Iacopini, Latora, Lucas, Patania, Young & Petri
papers.title: Networks beyond Pairwise Interactions: Structure and Dynamics
papers.why: Surveys hypergraphs and simplicial complexes for group interactions. Higher-order networks are one of the field's main frontiers.

more.authors: Milo, Shen-Orr, Itzkovitz, Kashtan, Chklovskii & Alon
more.title: Network Motifs: Simple Building Blocks of Complex Networks
more.why: Found small subgraphs that recur far more often than chance and linked them to function. Motif analysis remains standard in gene regulation and neural network studies.

more.title: Maximizing the Spread of Influence through a Social Network
more.venue: Proceedings of the 9th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
more.why: Framed choosing seed users to maximize spread as a submodular optimization problem with guarantees. Viral marketing, intervention seeding and diffusion research still build on it.

more.title: Complex Contagions and the Weakness of Long Ties
more.why: Showed that behaviors needing reinforcement from several contacts spread through clustered ties, not long bridges. This qualifies Granovetter and is central to current social contagion research.

more.title: Fast Unfolding of Communities in Large Networks
more.venue: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
more.why: Introduced the Louvain algorithm for optimizing modularity on networks with millions of nodes. It and its Leiden successor are still among the most used community-detection tools.

more.title: Power-Law Distributions in Empirical Data
more.why: Gave rigorous methods for fitting and testing power laws and showed many claimed ones fail. It is the standard method whenever heavy tails are claimed.

more.title: Community Detection in Graphs
more.why: The comprehensive review of community detection methods, benchmarks and pitfalls. Still the main entry point to the most studied problem in network science.

more.title: Stochastic Blockmodels and Community Structure in Networks
more.why: Added degree correction to the stochastic block model so it fits real networks. It made principled statistical inference the leading approach to community detection.

more.title: Temporal Networks
more.why: Reviewed networks whose links appear and disappear over time and showed timing changes spreading and reachability. It founded temporal network analysis as its own subfield.

more.title: Scale-Free Networks Are Rare
more.why: Tested nearly a thousand real networks and found strong power-law degree distributions are rare. It reignited the debate over one of the field's best-known claims.

more.title: Simplicial Models of Social Contagion
more.why: Showed that group interactions can make contagion explosive and bistable, unlike pairwise models. A key early result for higher-order network dynamics.

fields.lead: Combining robust and optimal control with learning from data, safety guarantees and distributed coordination.

papers.title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems
papers.venue: Journal of Basic Engineering (Transactions of the ASME)
papers.why: Introduced the recursive state estimator now called the Kalman filter. It runs in navigation, robotics and forecasting everywhere, and its extensions are still developed.

papers.title: Guaranteed Margins for LQG Regulators
papers.why: A one-page counterexample showing optimal LQG controllers can have arbitrarily small robustness margins. It started robust control and still warns against trusting optimality alone.

papers.title: Feedback and Optimal Sensitivity: Model Reference Transformations, Multiplicative Seminorms, and Approximate Inverses
papers.why: Posed control design as minimizing worst-case sensitivity, which led to H-infinity control. Robust control still uses this formulation.

papers.title: State-Space Solutions to Standard H2 and H-infinity Control Problems
papers.why: Gave practical Riccati-equation solutions for H-infinity design. Made robust control computable and remains standard.

papers.title: Constrained Model Predictive Control: Stability and Optimality
papers.why: Set the conditions under which MPC is stable and handles constraints. MPC is the dominant advanced control method in industry and robotics.

papers.title: Consensus Problems in Networks of Agents with Switching Topology and Time-Delays
papers.why: Gave a graph-theoretic analysis of agents agreeing through local communication. The basis of multi-agent and distributed control.

papers.title: Discovering Governing Equations from Data by Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.why: SINDy finds interpretable equations from data using sparse regression. A main approach in data-driven modeling.

papers.title: Control Barrier Function Based Quadratic Programs for Safety Critical Systems
papers.why: Combined barrier functions and quadratic programs to enforce safety in real time. Widely used to make learned controllers safe.

papers.title: A Tour of Reinforcement Learning: The View from Continuous Control
papers.venue: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
papers.why: Compared reinforcement learning with classical control on shared benchmarks. It framed the current merger of the two fields.

papers.title: On the Sample Complexity of the Linear Quadratic Regulator
papers.why: Gave non-asymptotic bounds on learning a controller from data. Defines how 'learning for control' theory is done now.

more.title: Smooth Stabilization Implies Coprime Factorization
more.why: Introduced input-to-state stability, a way to measure how disturbances affect nonlinear systems. ISS is now the standard language for robustness and interconnection of nonlinear systems.

more.title: The Complex Structured Singular Value
more.why: The reference treatment of mu analysis for systems with structured uncertainty. It is still used to certify robustness in aerospace and other safety-critical designs.

more.title: Coordination of Groups of Mobile Autonomous Agents Using Nearest Neighbor Rules
more.why: Proved that agents following the Vicsek nearest-neighbor rule reach agreement under changing connections. It helped found multi-agent coordination theory used in robot swarms.

more.title: Safety Verification of Hybrid Systems Using Barrier Certificates
more.venue: Hybrid Systems: Computation and Control (HSCC 2004), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
more.why: Introduced barrier certificates, functions that prove a system never enters unsafe states, found by sum-of-squares optimization. Control barrier functions and safe learning grow directly from it.

more.title: A Note on Persistency of Excitation
more.why: Showed that one sufficiently rich data trajectory describes all behaviors of a linear system. This 'fundamental lemma' is the basis of today's direct data-driven control.

more.title: Safe Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with Stability Guarantees
more.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
more.why: Combined Lyapunov stability analysis with Gaussian-process models so an agent can explore without leaving a safe region. A key reference for safe reinforcement learning in robotics.

more.title: Global Convergence of Policy Gradient Methods for the Linear Quadratic Regulator
more.venue: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML)
more.why: Proved that policy gradient reaches the optimal LQR controller despite a nonconvex landscape. It opened the theory of policy optimization for control problems.

more.title: Data-Enabled Predictive Control: In the Shallows of the DeePC
more.why: Built predictive control directly from recorded data matrices, skipping system identification. DeePC is now a leading data-driven control method, tested on power systems and robots.

more.title: Formulas for Data-Driven Control: Stabilization, Optimality, and Robustness
more.why: Gave controllers computed straight from data through linear matrix inequalities. Central to the current theory of direct data-driven control.

more.title: Learning-Based Model Predictive Control: Toward Safe Learning in Control
more.venue: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
more.why: Reviewed how learned models and safety filters are being combined with MPC. A map of where learning-for-control research stands.

fields.lead: Finding principles such as scaling, criticality, collective behavior and tipping points that hold across biological, social, economic and climate systems, and testing them against data.

papers.title: More Is Different
papers.why: Argued each level of organization has its own laws not deducible in practice from the level below. The manifesto of emergence that complexity science still cites to justify itself.

papers.title: Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow
papers.why: Showed a simple deterministic model can be unpredictable because of sensitivity to initial conditions. Limits on prediction in weather and other systems are still framed by it.

papers.title: Dynamic Models of Segregation
papers.why: Showed mild individual preferences can produce strong segregation. The template for agent-based models in social science.

papers.title: Simple Mathematical Models with Very Complicated Dynamics
papers.why: Showed the logistic map produces chaos and urged scientists to expect it in simple models. Still shapes how ecologists and others read irregular data.

papers.title: Self-Organized Criticality: An Explanation of 1/f Noise
papers.why: Proposed that systems drive themselves to critical states with avalanches of all sizes. How widely it applies, from earthquakes to brains, is still argued.

papers.title: A General Model for the Origin of Allometric Scaling Laws in Biology
papers.why: Derived quarter-power scaling of metabolism from branching networks. Influential and still contested, it inspired scaling studies of cities and firms.

papers.title: Growth, Innovation, Scaling, and the Pace of Life in Cities
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.why: Found that urban output scales superlinearly with population while infrastructure scales sublinearly. Founded the science of cities and is still being tested.

papers.title: The Product Space Conditions the Development of Nations
papers.why: Mapped which products countries can move into based on related capabilities. Economic complexity is now used in development policy.

papers.authors: Scheffer, Bascompte, Brock, Brovkin, Carpenter, Dakos, Held, van Nes, Rietkerk & Sugihara
papers.title: Early-Warning Signals for Critical Transitions
papers.why: Showed systems approaching tipping points slow down in detectable ways. Used today to monitor climate, ecosystem and other tipping risks.

papers.title: Are Biological Systems Poised at Criticality?
papers.why: Examined evidence that neurons, flocks and proteins sit near critical points. The question remains one of the field's most active debates.

more.title: The Architecture of Complexity
more.venue: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society
more.why: Argued that complex systems are built from nearly decomposable hierarchies of subsystems, which makes them evolvable. It remains the standard reference for modularity in biology, organizations and engineering.

more.title: Metabolic Stability and Epigenesis in Randomly Constructed Genetic Nets
more.why: Modeled gene regulation with random Boolean networks and found ordered, stable behavior near a critical point. These models are still used to study cell types and criticality in biology.

more.title: Will a Large Complex System Be Stable?
more.why: Used random matrix theory to show that large, densely connected ecosystems should become unstable. The diversity-stability debate in ecology is still organized around this result.

more.title: Competing Technologies, Increasing Returns, and Lock-In by Historical Events
more.why: Showed that with increasing returns, small chance events can lock a market into an inferior technology. It is the basis of path dependence arguments in economics and technology policy.

more.title: Novel Type of Phase Transition in a System of Self-Driven Particles
more.why: Showed that particles following a simple alignment rule undergo a transition to collective motion. It founded the physics of active matter and remains the base model for flocking.

more.title: From Kuramoto to Crawford: Exploring the Onset of Synchronization in Populations of Coupled Oscillators
more.why: Reviewed how the Kuramoto model explains spontaneous synchronization and its mathematics. Synchronization in power grids, brains and biological rhythms is still analyzed with it.

more.title: Interaction Ruling Animal Collective Behavior Depends on Topological Rather than Metric Distance: Evidence from a Field Study
more.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
more.why: Reconstructed real starling flocks in 3D and found each bird tracks about seven neighbors regardless of distance. It changed how collective-motion models are built and tested against data.
more.note: Exact title wording recalled from memory.

more.authors: Lenton, Held, Kriegler, Hall, Lucht, Rahmstorf & Schellnhuber
more.title: Tipping Elements in the Earth's Climate System
more.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
more.why: Identified climate subsystems, such as ice sheets and the Amazon, that could shift abruptly past a threshold. It defines the list of tipping elements that climate risk research still monitors and revises.

more.title: The Building Blocks of Economic Complexity
more.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
more.why: Introduced the method of reflections, which infers a country's hidden capabilities from what it exports. The resulting economic complexity index predicts growth better than many standard indicators and is now widely used in development work.

more.title: Systemic Risk in Banking Ecosystems
more.why: Applied ideas from ecological network stability to contagion between banks. It shaped post-2008 thinking on why highly connected, homogeneous financial systems are fragile.
